titleEn: Why achieving your goals can leave you feeling so empty
titleZh: 为什么实现目标后，反而会感到空虚？
method: Machine reference translation with paragraph alignment; not manually certified.

paragraphs.en: When Anne Carson learned she had won the Nobel Prize in literature, she was in Iceland, where, according to the Swedish Academy, she was “listening to the wind.”
paragraphs.zh: 当安妮卡森得知自己获得诺贝尔文学奖时，她正在冰岛，据瑞典学院称，她在那里“听风”

paragraphs.en: Carson didn’t answer her phone right away, silencing it until her husband persuaded her to call back. Her verdict on the academy’s choice: “I think you’re all insane.”
paragraphs.zh: 卡森没有马上接电话，直到她的丈夫说服她再打过来，她对学院的选择做出了结论：“我认为你们都疯了。”

paragraphs.en: Whatever she felt in the moment, there is an irony in Carson’s Nobel win. The highest award in literature has gone to a writer who has spent her career exploring the emptiness of a desire fulfilled.
paragraphs.zh: 无论她当时有什么感受，卡森获得诺贝尔奖都有一种讽刺意味。文学最高奖颁给了一位一生都在探索欲望实现后的空虚的作家。

paragraphs.en: The honor coincides with the 40th anniversary of the publication of her first book, “Eros the Bittersweet,” a meditation on desire.
paragraphs.zh: 这一荣誉恰逢她的第一本书《苦乐参半的厄洛斯》出版40周年，这本书是对欲望的沉思。

paragraphs.en: In it, Carson argues that desire begins with a void – with wanting what we don’t have. She traces how this feeling of absence shapes love, reading, writing and thinking, activities that renew themselves precisely because they are never complete.
paragraphs.zh: 在书中，卡森认为，欲望始于空虚--渴望我们没有的东西。她追溯了这种缺失感如何塑造了爱、阅读、写作和思考，这些活动之所以能自我更新，正是因为它们永远不会完成。

paragraphs.en: The philosopher and the top
paragraphs.zh: 哲学家和顶级

paragraphs.en: “Eros” begins with a brief preface on Franz Kafka’s “The Top,” a story about a philosopher who spends his time around children so he can chase their spinning tops. When a child sets a top in motion, the philosopher snatches it, believing that understanding any small thing, even a spinning top, would be enough to understand everything.
paragraphs.zh: 《爱欲》一开始是弗朗茨·Kafka（Franz Kafka）的《陀螺》（The Top）的简短序言。《陀螺》讲述的是一个哲学家把时间花在孩子们身上，以便追逐他们旋转的陀螺。当孩子们把陀螺弄起来时，哲学家会抓住它，他相信理解任何一件小事，哪怕是一个旋转的陀螺，都足以理解一切。

paragraphs.en: While the top spins, the philosopher is filled with hope, but as soon as he grasps it, he is repelled by the dumb piece of wood. He throws it down and waits for the next child to spin a top.
paragraphs.zh: 陀螺旋转时，哲学家充满了希望，但他刚抓住陀螺，就被那块哑巴木头推开了，他把它扔了下来，等待下一个孩子旋转陀螺。

paragraphs.en: For Carson, the story is about why people love to fall in love. The philosopher is after what Carson calls an “impertinent stability in vertigo,” a state that is “itself delightful, a suspended moment of living hope.” The philosopher’s quest for knowledge, Carson cheekily concludes, is simply his pretext for chasing spinning tops. He is enchanted by the spinning itself, and even by his own enchantment – a spell that breaks the instant the top stops in his hand.
paragraphs.zh: 对卡森来说，这个故事是关于人们为什么喜欢坠入爱河。这位哲学家追求的是卡森所说的“眩晕中的不恰当的稳定性”，一种“本身令人愉快的、充满希望的悬置时刻”的状态。卡森厚颜无耻地总结说，哲学家对知识的追求只是他追逐旋转陀螺的借口。他被旋转本身迷住了，甚至是他自己的魔法--一个在陀螺停在他手中的瞬间就会打破的咒语。

paragraphs.en: Most people know a version of this: There is something animating about chasing a goal. But once attained, the framed degree fades into the wall, the promotion quickly loses its luster, and the plaque becomes another dumb piece of wood.
paragraphs.zh: 大多数人都知道这样一个版本：追逐目标是一件令人兴奋的事情，但一旦实现了目标，框架内的学位就会消失在墙上，晋升很快就会失去光彩，牌匾也会变成另一块哑巴木头。

paragraphs.en: The delight of wanting disappears in the having.
paragraphs.zh: 想要的快乐消失在拥有中。

paragraphs.en: A hole in the self
paragraphs.zh: 自我中的一个洞

paragraphs.en: Why does fulfillment so often feel like loss?
paragraphs.zh: 为什么成就感常常让人感觉像是失去？

paragraphs.en: Carson’s answer begins with the Greek word for erotic love, “eros,” which she explains denotes want or lack. Plato’s Socrates makes the same point in the “Symposium.” For the Greeks, no one desires what they already have.
paragraphs.zh: 卡森的回答是从希腊语中的“eros”开始的，她解释说，“eros”表示想要或缺乏。柏拉图的苏格拉底在《会饮篇》中也提出了同样的观点。对希腊人来说，没有人渴望他们已经拥有的东西。

paragraphs.en: Desire also opens up an absence. To long for someone or something is to discover our own edges, the chasm where the self ends and what is wanted begins. Eros reveals that we are incomplete – an awareness that causes the self to become undone, loosening at the joints.
paragraphs.zh: 欲望也会开启一种缺失。渴望某人或某事是发现我们自己的边缘，自我结束和想要的东西开始的鸿沟。爱欲揭示了我们是不完整的--一种导致自我变得不完整的意识，在关节处松动。

paragraphs.en: In one of her poems, the Greek poet Sappho called this experience “glukupikron,” or “sweetbitter.”
paragraphs.zh: 在她的一首诗中，希腊诗人萨福称这种经历为“glukupikron”，或“甜苦”。

paragraphs.en: Carson’s translation of the passage reads: “Eros once again limb-loosener whirls me / sweetbitter, impossible to fight off, creature stealing up.”
paragraphs.zh: 卡森对这段话的翻译是：“厄洛斯再一次让我四肢放松/甜蜜痛苦，无法击退，生物偷了起来。”

paragraphs.en: Sappho puts sweet first, Carson notes in “Eros,” but desire is not initially sweet and then bitter. Pleasure and pain arrive together, in the same body and at the same time, before the lover is even able to distinguish them.
paragraphs.zh: 卡森在《爱欲》一书中写道，萨福把甜蜜放在第一位，但欲望并不是先甜后苦的，快乐和痛苦在同一个身体上同时到来，甚至在爱人能够区分它们之前。

paragraphs.en: Carson extends this pattern to reading, writing and thinking. A reader approaches a text’s meaning but never masters it; every rereading turns up new meanings. The pleasure of understanding and the ache of incompleteness arrive together.
paragraphs.zh: 卡森将这种模式扩展到阅读、写和思考。读者接近文本的意义，但永远无法掌握它;每一次重新阅读都会产生新的意义。理解的乐趣和不完整的痛苦同时到来。

paragraphs.en: Writing works the same way. A good sentence both captures and conceals what the writer means. Thinking also runs on that doubled feeling, which is how the story of a philosopher chasing tops ended up in a book about love.
paragraphs.zh: 写作也是如此。一个好的句子既能抓住又能隐藏作者的意思。思考也是基于这种双重的感觉，这就是为什么一个哲学家追逐顶峰的故事最终会出现在一本关于爱情的书中。

paragraphs.en: The trouble with goals
paragraphs.zh: 目标的麻烦在于

paragraphs.en: The same bittersweet pattern also shows up somewhere far less romantic: at work. Meeting a deadline brings relief that is already hollow because the next one is waiting.
paragraphs.zh: 同样的甜蜜模式也出现在不那么浪漫的地方：工作中。赶在最后期限前完成任务带来的解脱已经是空洞的，因为下一个还在等着。

paragraphs.en: I discovered “Eros the Bittersweet” as a philosophy graduate student, when my goals were to read, write and think my way into questions I loved. Now I spend much of my day as a university administrator, where the quality of my work is measured in metrics and met deadlines. Somewhere along the way, my goals stopped being things I wanted and became things to check off.
paragraphs.zh: 在读哲学研究生时，我发现了"苦乐参半的爱神"，当时我的目标是阅读、写作，用自己的方式思考我喜欢的问题。现在，我每天的大部分时间都是作为一名大学行政人员，我的工作质量是以指标衡量的，并在最后期限内完成。在这条道路上的沿着，我的目标不再是我想要的东西，而是变成了需要检查的东西。

paragraphs.en: Today’s productivity culture chases tops of its own, but it looks less like Kafka’s philosopher than like Lucy and Ethel working at the chocolate factory in the 1952 “I Love Lucy” episode “Job Switching.” As the conveyor belt speeds up, the only way they can look like they’re keeping up is to stuff what they’ve missed into their mouths.
paragraphs.zh: 如今的生产力文化追求的是自己的最高水平，但它看起来不像Kafka笔下的哲学家，而更像1952年《我爱露西》（I Love Lucy）中的"工作转换"（Job Switching）一集中，露西和埃塞尔在巧克力工厂工作。随着传送带的加速，他们唯一能让自己看起来跟得上的方式就是把错过的东西塞进嘴里。

paragraphs.en: Few things capture this pressure more than the SMART goal. In 1981, management consultant George Doran proposed that goals be SMART: specific, measurable, assignable, realistic and time-related. The acronym spread through industries and disciplines as a model for strategic planning, project management, performance evaluations and personal goal-setting. It distills a wider creed: Set the target, sprint after it, hit it. Grasp the top, toss it, capture the next one, ad infinitum. Doran didn’t invent the impulse, but his acronym gave it a checklist.
paragraphs.zh: 没有什么比SMART目标更能体现这种压力了。1981年，管理顾问乔治多兰（George Doran）提出，目标应该是SMART的：具体、可衡量、可分配、现实和与时间相关。这个首字母缩略词作为战略规划、项目管理、绩效评估和个人目标设定的一种模式，在各个行业和学科中传播开来。它提炼出一个更广泛的信条：设定目标，追着它跑，击中它。抓住上面的东西，扔出去，抓住下一个，无穷无尽。多兰并没有发明冲动，但他的首字母缩略词给了它一个清单。

paragraphs.en: Carson’s account of desire helps explain why this creed leads to two kinds of emptiness.
paragraphs.zh: 卡森对欲望的描述有助于解释为什么这种信条会导致两种空虚。

paragraphs.en: The first comes from pursuing goals people never really desired. Inbox zero and a quarterly metric are goals in service of goals, the ultimate of which is productivity itself, which often simply ends up boosting someone else’s productivity.
paragraphs.zh: 第一个是追求人们从未真正想要的目标，零成本和季度指标是为目标服务的目标，最终是生产力本身，这往往只是提高了别人的生产力。

paragraphs.en: The second comes from goals people truly wanted. Psychologist Tal Ben-Shahar calls the letdown that follows the “arrival fallacy” – the belief that reaching a destination will bring lasting happiness.
paragraphs.zh: 第二种来自人们真正想要的目标。心理学家塔尔·本-沙哈尔称之为"到达谬误"--相信到达目的地会带来持久的幸福。

paragraphs.en: The Greeks offer another kind of striving, one that locates pleasure in the pursuit itself rather than in the prize. In Plato’s “Phaedrus,” Socrates describes eros as giving the soul wings and treats philosophy as a love of wisdom no one can own.
paragraphs.zh: 希腊人提供了另一种奋斗方式，他们把快乐放在追求本身，而不是奖品中。在柏拉图的《斐德罗篇》中，苏格拉底把爱欲描述为给灵魂插上翅膀，把哲学看作是对智慧的热爱，没有人能拥有。

paragraphs.en: Centuries later, philosopher Alasdair MacIntyre distinguished external goods, such as money and status, from goods internal to a practice, such as a farmer’s growing mastery of her land or an architect’s pursuit of elegant, functional design. MacIntyre’s example, in his 1981 book “After Virtue,” is a child paid in candy to learn chess. As long as she plays for the candy, she has every reason to cheat. Only when she comes to love the game does she gain what chess itself can give: a particular kind of analytical skill, strategic imagination and competitive intensity.
paragraphs.zh: 几个世纪后，哲学家阿拉斯代尔·麦金太尔（Alasdair MacIntyre）区分了金钱和地位等外在商品和农民对土地的日益掌握或建筑师对优雅实用设计的追求等内在商品。麦金太尔在1981年的《追求美德》（After Virtue）一书中举了一个例子，一个孩子用糖果学习国际象棋。只要她为糖果而玩，她有充分的理由作弊。2只有当她爱上这项运动时，她才能获得国际象棋本身所能给予的东西：一种特殊的分析技巧、战略想象力和竞争强度。

paragraphs.en: To Socrates, MacIntyre and Carson, external goods get used up as they are won. Internal goods deepen the longer we pursue them.
paragraphs.zh: 对苏格拉底、麦金太尔和卡森来说，外在的好处在我们赢得的时候就被消耗殆尽，而内在的好处在我们追求它们的时候就变得更加深刻。

paragraphs.en: Keeping desire alive means choosing pursuits that can never be finished – a craft, a field of study, a relationship – and letting the gap between reaching and grasping stay open. In this way, the lack that can hollow us out can also be what moves us.
paragraphs.zh: 保持欲望的活力意味着选择永远无法完成的追求--一门手艺、一个研究领域、一段关系--让达到和把握之间的差距保持开放。这样，让我们空洞的缺乏也可以成为让我们感动的东西。

paragraphs.en: Carson was handed the highest prize in literature. Yet the picture the Swedish Academy left us with is of a writer standing in the Icelandic wind, attending to a force of nature that no one can catch.
paragraphs.zh: 卡森获得了最高的文学奖，但瑞典文学院留给我们的画面是一位作家站在冰岛的风中，注意到一种无人能捕捉的自然力量。
